0.long_answer: Mutations in the SCN4A gene affect the function of the NaV1.4 sodium channel in skeletal muscle cells. Under normal conditions, this channel permits the rapid influx of sodium ions from the extracellular space into the muscle cell, which is essential for initiating and propagating action potentials necessary for muscle contraction. In hypokalemic periodic paralysis caused by defective SCN4A channels, this sodium influx is disrupted. The impaired sodium flow contributes to abnormal muscle excitability and episodic muscle weakness, a hallmark of the condition.
